verdict.rationale: Pylon's API reference renders GitBook's in-page "Test it" runner on each endpoint, driven by a complete, publicly downloadable OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec, so users can explore the reference and run requests from it. The runner needs the caller's own bearer token, and the spec's only servers are the US/EU production APIs, so every example call hits live production data with no sandbox or mock environment. missing for 10: sandbox or mock server for safe runnable examples, try-it access without a production token, independent or hands-on corroboration of the runner experience.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The API reference renders GitBook's in-page "Test it" runner per endpoint, driven by the published spec.
The runner requires the caller's own bearer token and the spec's only servers are the US/EU production APIs, so requests execute against production.
The GitBook docs render every endpoint page from this spec URL and embed the per-endpoint OpenAPI JSON in their markdown mirrors.
